title: The Most Important Question in Any Leadership Interview
author: The Business Leader Daily
summary: The author argues that every leader you hire either expands or limits your impact, so the most revealing interview questions probe a candidate's growth mindset and their track record of developing others. Beyond assessing competency and character, the piece recommends asking what the candidate has done in the past year to improve as a leader and to develop the leaders on their team, looking for concrete answers over vague claims. The signature question, adopted after the author was once asked it, is "What does your leadership tree look like?", a review of how direct reports' careers progressed both during and after their time together, revealing whether a candidate truly builds future leaders.
points: Every hire either expands or limits your impact, so hiring leaders who develop other leaders compounds your leadership capacity.
Asking what a candidate has done in the past year to improve as a leader tests whether they invest in themselves; strong answers are concrete, not vague.
Asking what they have done to develop the leaders on their team reveals whether they architect growth or treat it as someone else's job.
The "leadership tree" question examines how direct reports' careers progressed both during and after working with the candidate.
A track record of developing other leaders increases the likelihood a hire will bring the impact and collective success you're looking for.
quotes: If you hire a growth-focused leader who develops other leaders, your potential for impact grows. Conversely, if you hire a leader who fails to develop others, your long-term results may suffer.
This question reveals whether they view leadership development as something they architect or something that someone else takes care of.
It’s the measure of who your leaders became, both while you led them and after they moved on. Did they grow under your watch? Did they keep growing afterward?
Remember, great leaders don't just achieve results on their own; they amplify leadership capacity, transforming their team’s potential into collective success.
A leadership tree review assesses whether you successfully developed future leaders while working with them and whether they sustained that development after moving on.
